newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian press says Berisha will resign, left wins.
newsitem.headline: Albanian press says Berisha will resign, left wins.

text.p: Most Albanian newspapers said on Tuesday President Sali Berisha would quit after rival Socialists appeared to have won a general election, but others said the left came to power backed by armed gangs.
"Berisha announced his farewell and invited his supporters to keep calm," the independent daily Gazeta Shqiptare reported in its first edition since Sunday's election.

The paper said Berisha chose to appear personally on television to concede the defeat of his Democratic Party rather than do so through a spokesman's statement. The news was greeted by volleys of gunfire in the streets of both central and suburban Tirana.
Koha Jone, the biggest circulation daily, which has been critical of Berisha's administration, described the election as an historic lesson to those who chose to govern by authoritarian rule.

"In a day that was more peaceful than expected, the crushing majority of two million voters opted to oust a political class that ruled with an iron hand during the years of Albania's transition (from communism)," the paper said in an editorial.
The daily paid tribute to the police, who demonstrated their professionalism in observing the law and took no sides during the polling. "Police were the real stars," a headline read.
But pro-Democratic Party newspapers accused the Socialist Party, reformed heirs to the communist party, of using armed supporters to manipulate the vote.

"The Democratic Party did not get good results because the Socialist Party obliged voters to back them through the force of arms in almost all areas," the Democratic Party daily Rilindja Demokratike said.
The paper said over 20 Democrat candidates would win in a second round due on July 6 in order to restore confidence in the party and not to allow parliament to be dominated by "communists".
"Acknowledging the election results, the Democratic Party showed to the Socialist Party how it should behave within a short period of time," the newspaper said.

Albania, a newspaper close to the Democrats, said that the country had restored the monarchy in a referendum held on Sunday. It published pictures of exiled king Leka alongside Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha, who ruled the Balkan state until his death in 1985 -- five years before communism was toppled in a popular revolt.
The paper reported comments by a Western analyst who said the international community should have allowed more time for Albania to carry out a process of national reconciliation.
"Elections were held now because the international community wanted to leave Albania as soon as possible and not because it wanted solve the problems of Albania," the paper said.
A headline in the newspaper Indipendent said that communism had finally died in the general election.
"Berisha tried to uproot communism with anti-communism and revived a lot of communist methods...He was perhaps the last communist," Indipendent said in an editorial.
